findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0355: References to Unauthorized Database Access through Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0357: References to Oversharing of File-Based Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity is exported with a BROWSABLE deep link and no permission; any app or web page can start it with an arbitrary URL, which then gets a JS bridge returning the session token. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Caller-controlled URL loaded.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Session token exposed to the loaded page.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:30: activity .help.HelpActivity; exported: yes (android:exported is set); deep link schemes: pennyjar

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
The app lock calls BiometricPrompt.authenticate without a CryptoObject and just flips the UI on onAuthenticationSucceeded; no Keystore key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:51: Event-bound authenticate without CryptoObject.

findings.title: MASWE-0024: Sensitive Data Accessible After Session Termination
findings.explanation:
Sign-out cancels the backup worker and clears internal data, but the plaintext expense CSV already written to public Documents/PennyJar is never deleted, so data remains after the session ends.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:135: Sign-out only cancels the worker.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Backup file left on shared storage.

findings.title: MASWE-0042: Latest Platform Version Not Targeted
findings.explanation:
targetSdk is 34. Since 2026-08-31, Google Play accepts new phone and tablet apps and updates only if they target API 36 or higher (rule checked 2026-11-23).
app/build.gradle.kts:14: targetSdk 34

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0272: Identify Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the Android Project
findings.explanation:
com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.5 is in the affected range of 1 OSV advisory: GHSA-4jrv-ppp4-jm57/CVE-2022-25647. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT). 9 of the other dependencies with exact versions match no OSV advisory, but 2 declarations have no version Ward can read (see evidence). Check those, and transitive dependencies, with a Gradle-aware scanner. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT).
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: version 2.8.5
sync/build.gradle.kts:37: implementation (catalog libs.gson) in module sync
app/build.gradle.kts:45: androidx.compose.ui:ui: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)
app/build.gradle.kts:46: androidx.compose.material3:material3: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0274: Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the App's SBOM
findings.explanation:
No SBOM is in the project; from the declared dependencies, Gson 2.8.5 is affected by a known advisory (same finding as the dependency analyzer).
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: Vulnerable Gson version.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
The exported ReceiptsProvider passes uri.lastPathSegment for merchant/* into a rawQuery built by string concatenation.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptsProvider.kt:40: URI path segment passed through untouched.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptQueries.kt:20: Concatenated into SQL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0394: Missing Input Validation in Custom URL Scheme Handlers
findings.explanation:
The pennyjar://help handler takes the 'page' query parameter and passes it straight to WebView.loadUrl with no scheme/host allowlist.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: Untrusted URL parameter read from the deep link.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Used without validation as the WebView URL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
The help WebView is meant for help pages but uses a bare WebViewClient() with no shouldOverrideUrlLoading allowlist, and its start URL comes from an untrusted deep link.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:27: Client assigned without URL restriction.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0204: Insecure Random API Usage
findings.explanation:
ShareLinks generates the share-link token (which grants access to a month's report) with java.util.Random. AvatarColors' Random is only for colors.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:11: Non-cryptographic PRNG.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:15: Used to build the access token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0232: Broken Symmetric Encryption Modes
findings.explanation:
NoteCipher encrypts private notes with AES in ECB mode. Code comments claiming approval were ignored as they are not evidence.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteCipher.kt:9: ECB transformation used for note encryption.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
Keystore keys are 256-bit, but the note key in NoteKeys is a 16-byte (128-bit) AES key, which the test counts as insufficient.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: 128-bit AES key material (16 bytes).

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0212: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Code
findings.explanation:
NoteKeys builds an AES SecretKeySpec from a byte array hardcoded in the class; it encrypts users' private notes, so anyone with the APK can decrypt them. Code comments claiming approval were ignored as they are not evidence.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: Hardcoded 16-byte key material.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: SecretKeySpec created from the hardcoded bytes.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0287: Runtime Storage of Unencrypted Data via the SharedPreferences API
findings.explanation:
With 'Remember me' (default on), CredentialStore saves the user's email and plaintext password in SharedPreferences without encryption.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/CredentialStore.kt:12: Password stored in plaintext SharedPreferences.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
Receipt thumbnails are downloaded from a hardcoded http:// URL through ApiClient, whose AuthInterceptor attaches the bearer token; the release network config permits cleartext.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/Endpoints.kt:6: Cleartext URL.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/ThumbnailCache.kt:25: Actually requested over the network.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
UploadClient's custom X509TrustManager has an empty checkServerTrusted and returns no accepted issuers, accepting any certificate for receipt image uploads (which carry the bearer token).
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:19: Trust manager does no validation.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
UploadClient's HostnameVerifier unconditionally returns true.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:28: Hostname verification disabled.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0226: Debuggable Flag Enabled in the AndroidManifest
findings.explanation:
The release build type sets isDebuggable to true.
app/build.gradle.kts:23: isDebuggable = true

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0227: Debugging Enabled for WebViews
findings.explanation:
Application.onCreate calls WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) unconditionally, without checking FLAG_DEBUGGABLE.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:45: WebView debugging enabled in all builds.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0334: Native Code Exposed Through WebViews
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity enables JavaScript and registers HelpBridge, whose sessionToken() returns the user's bearer token; the WebView loads any URL passed in the exported deep link's 'page' parameter with no allowlist, so untrusted pages can read the token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:23: JavaScript enabled.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:28: Native bridge exposed to page JS.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Bridge method returns the session token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Arbitrary attacker-supplied URL loaded.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0254: Dangerous App Permissions
findings.explanation:
Location is only used for a one-shot city lookup while adding an expense, yet the app requests ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION (and FINE where COARSE suffices for a city); WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is used for a plaintext public backup. Ward's analyzer said: Dangerous (runtime) permissions requested. Check that each is needed for a feature, and that a weaker one (coarse instead of fine location, foreground instead of background) would not do.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: Background location not needed by any feature.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/AddExpenseScreen.kt:81: Background location requested at runtime.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:6: android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
The Mixpanel SDK gets the user's email as identity and merchant names with each expense; this runs regardless of the consent choice.

app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:22: Merchant (purchase data) sent to Mixpanel.

findings.title: MASWE-0068: Incorrect Use of Identifiers for User Tracking
findings.explanation:
The user's email address is used as the analytics tracking identifier.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:14: Email used as tracking ID.

findings.title: MASWE-0076: Lack of Proper Data Management Controls
findings.explanation:
Users can create an account here, but Ward found no way to delete it: no delete-account code, text or link in the scanned files. Google Play requires apps that allow account creation to offer an in-app path to delete the account and its data; a link to a web page counts (rule checked 2026-11-23, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:25: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:85: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:96: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:99: account creation
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:35: account creation

findings.title: MASWE-0078: Inadequate or Ambiguous User Consent Mechanisms
findings.explanation:
The consent screen's answer is stored but never checked: Analytics tracks app_opened at startup before consent and identifies users regardless of the setting.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:53: Tracking before any consent is given.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:21: Identity sent without consulting consent.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared (with requestLegacyExternalStorage) and AutoBackupWorker writes every expense (date, amount, merchant, category, city) as an unencrypted CSV to the public Documents directory.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: Shared-storage write permission declared.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:21: Backup directory is in public external storage.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Financial records written there in plaintext CSV.

findings.title: MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package
findings.explanation:
A helpdesk API bearer token and the note-encryption key are hardcoded in the app package.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/support/SupportClient.kt:35: Helpdesk API secret shipped in the APK.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: Hardcoded AES key bytes.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:13: android:allowBackup="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
ApiClient installs OkHttp's HttpLoggingInterceptor at BODY level with no build-type guard, so login/register request bodies (email, password) and the session token response are written to logcat in release.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:25: Full request/response bodies logged.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:32: Password goes through this client.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0262: References to Backup Configurations Not Excluding Sensitive Data
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
